title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was used to create non-consensual sexually explicit images of a real person. The attacker obtained photos from the victim's social media accounts, used AI tools to create obscene morphed images, and distributed them across multiple platforms under fake identities. The deployment failure was complete absence of safeguards: no requirement for identity verification, no detection of misuse patterns, and no technical measures to prevent the creation or distribution of non-consensual intimate imagery.

This is a straightforward case of a tool used intentionally for harm rather than a system failure in the technical sense. The victim discovered the abuse through reports from others, then alerted law enforcement. To prevent similar incidents would have required the AI system itself to refuse requests for generating non-consensual sexual imagery, and the platforms used for distribution to have stronger identity verification and content moderation.

It is not established what specific AI services or tools were used, or what technical measures, if any, those systems had in place to detect or prevent this type of misuse.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and sharing sexually explicit AI-generated images of a college acquaintance. Bansal, a BTech graduate in Electronics and Communication Engineering, obtained photos from the woman's private social media accounts and used artificial intelligence technology to create obscene morphed images. He then distributed this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using several Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The victim, also 22 years old, discovered the abuse when she received messages from anonymous Instagram accounts alerting her to the morphed images circulating on Discord servers. She filed a complaint with the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi. During their investigation, police analyzed digital footprints and traced the fake profiles, eventually identifying and apprehending Bansal. He admitted to knowing the victim from college and revealed that personal resentment had developed between them. Police recovered a mobile phone, two SIM cards, and other digital evidence related to the case, with investigation continuing.
